body:
### Process detection logic triplicated across all three plugins **Medium Severity** The tmux TTY → `ps` lookup → PID check logic (~45 lines) is copy-pasted across all three agent plugins, differing only in a hardcoded process name string (`"aider"`, `"codex"`, `"claude"`). Each agent already exposes a `processName` property with this value, so a shared parameterized helper (e.g. in core or a shared utils module) could replace all three copies. A bug fix or platform compatibility change to this subprocess logic would need to be applied in three places.
Additional Locations (2) - [`packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts#L82-L128`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/ce9ee17c4901cf595b168c6fc6b4e7d2d775dc61/packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts#L82-L128) - [`packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts#L247-L298`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/ce9ee17c4901cf595b168c6fc6b4e7d2d775dc61/packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts#L247-L298)

### Shell escape utility duplicated across all three plugins **Low Severity** The `shellEscape` function is identically defined in all three agent plugins. Since all three packages already depend on `@agent-orchestrator/core`, this utility could live there (or in a shared utils module) to avoid maintaining three copies.
Additional Locations (2) - [`packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts#L33-L36`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/ce9ee17c4901cf595b168c6fc6b4e7d2d775dc61/packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts#L33-L36) - [`packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts#L205-L208`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/ce9ee17c4901cf595b168c6fc6b4e7d2d775dc61/packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts#L205-L208)

### Polling skips runtime death transitions **Medium Severity** `pollAll()` filters out sessions already marked `killed` by `sessionManager.list()`, so dead-runtime sessions never reach `checkSession()`. That prevents `lifecycle-manager.ts` from emitting `session.killed`, updating metadata via `updateMetadata`, and running any reaction logic for that transition during normal polling.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/core/src/session-manager.ts#L303-L306`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/20693f742ddff830b2c58fb994bb1e744621f9c1/packages/core/src/session-manager.ts#L303-L306)

### Reaction retries bypassed on first send failure **Medium Severity** In `executeReaction()`, a `send-to-agent` failure immediately calls `notifyHuman()` and returns `escalated: true`, even when `ReactionConfig.retries` allows more attempts. This makes `retries` ineffective for transient `sessionManager.send()` failures.

### Successful reactions still trigger escalation limits **Medium Severity** `executeReaction()` increments `tracker.attempts` before execution and uses it for escalation, but never resets it after success. This makes `retries` behave like total event count, so later successful `send-to-agent` reactions can be escalated even without prior failures.

### Spawn failures leak runtime and workspace **High Severity** After `runtime.create()` succeeds, failures in `writeMetadata()` or `agent.postLaunchSetup()` are not rolled back. `spawn()` throws but leaves the runtime session and workspace alive, creating orphaned resources and inconsistent state with no session metadata.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/core/src/session-manager.ts#L228-L235`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/20693f742ddff830b2c58fb994bb1e744621f9c1/packages/core/src/session-manager.ts#L228-L235)

### Kill omits cleanup when project config missing **Medium Severity** `kill()` only destroys runtime/workspace when `config.projects[projectId]` exists. If a session references a removed or renamed project, it skips destruction and still calls `deleteMetadata()`, leaving the actual runtime/workspace running but removing the only tracking record.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/core/src/session-manager.ts#L359-L361`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/20693f742ddff830b2c58fb994bb1e744621f9c1/packages/core/src/session-manager.ts#L359-L361)

### Shell injection via unescaped single quotes in printf **High Severity** The `printf` command in the `write text` AppleScript uses `${safe}` (AppleScript-escaped only) inside a shell single-quoted context. `escapeAppleScript` only handles backslashes and double quotes — it does not escape single quotes. If the session name contains a `'`, it breaks out of the shell single-quoted string, leading to command injection. The `tmux attach` part correctly uses `${shellSafe}`, but the `printf` part does not.

### Duplicated `escapeAppleScript` across two plugin packages **Low Severity** `escapeAppleScript` is defined identically in both `notifier-desktop` and `terminal-iterm2`. Duplicating this security-sensitive escaping logic increases the risk that a future bug fix is applied to one copy but not the other. Extracting it into a shared utility (or the `@agent-orchestrator/core` package) would ensure consistent behavior.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/plugins/notifier-desktop/src/index.ts#L21-L24`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/eccbbe1f2f935b14b66fd7a9ea10b5d5e07974f1/packages/plugins/notifier-desktop/src/index.ts#L21-L24)

### Attention level misclassifies sessions with `reviewDecision: "none"` **High Severity** `getAttentionLevel` only checks `pr.reviewDecision === "pending"` for the warning zone, but `"none"` is also a "needs review" state. Both `getAlerts` in `SessionCard` and `getMockStats` correctly handle `"pending" || "none"`, but `getAttentionLevel` omits `"none"`. This causes sessions like `frontend-5` (annotated as `// WARNING`) to land in the "ok" zone instead of "warning", while still displaying a "needs review" alert tag and being counted in the stats bar's "need review" number.
Additional Locations (2) - [`packages/web/src/components/SessionCard.tsx#L277-L278`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/a58f3dd6008b6e61f9b09797a547e3ec3354110c/packages/web/src/components/SessionCard.tsx#L277-L278) - [`packages/web/src/lib/mock-data.ts#L409-L410`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/a58f3dd6008b6e61f9b09797a547e3ec3354110c/packages/web/src/lib/mock-data.ts#L409-L410)

### ACTION zone uses green color instead of orange **Medium Severity** The PR spec defines the color scheme as "ACTION (orange)" but the `action` zone config in `AttentionZone` uses `var(--color-accent-green)` and `borderColorByLevel` in `SessionCard` uses `border-l-[var(--color-accent-green)]`. This makes the ACTION zone visually indistinguishable in meaning from a "success" state, undermining the attention-zone priority signaling.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/web/src/components/SessionCard.tsx#L26-L27`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/a58f3dd6008b6e61f9b09797a547e3ec3354110c/packages/web/src/components/SessionCard.tsx#L26-L27)

### SessionDetail date rendering causes hydration mismatch **Medium Severity** `SessionDetail` calls `new Date(session.createdAt).toLocaleString()` directly in the render body for the "Created" and "Last Activity" info cards. Since this is a `"use client"` component, it's still server-rendered initially, and `toLocaleString()` produces locale/timezone-dependent output. In production, where server and client locales differ, this creates a React hydration mismatch. The `Dashboard` component explicitly avoids this exact problem with a `ClientTimestamp` pattern using `useState` + `useEffect`, but that pattern wasn't applied here.

### SSE route missing dynamic export will be cached **High Severity** The SSE endpoint `GET` handler takes no `Request` parameter and the file has no `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` declaration. In Next.js App Router, GET route handlers without a `Request` parameter are treated as static and cached by default. This means the streaming response will be evaluated once and cached — the SSE endpoint won't create a fresh stream per client, completely breaking real-time event delivery. Every Next.js SSE tutorial shows this directive as required.

### Process name substring match causes false positives **Medium Severity** The condition `args.includes("/claude")` performs a substring match, so it falsely matches any process whose path contains `/claude` as a prefix — e.g., `/usr/bin/claude-desktop`, `/path/to/claudette`. This can cause `isProcessRunning` and `detectActivity` to incorrectly report a dead session as alive. The same issue affects the aider (`/aider`) and codex (`/codex`) plugins. Using `args.endsWith("/processName")` instead of `args.includes("/processName")` would fix the false-positive matching. Note that `args.includes("/claude ")` (condition 3) is also fully redundant since it's a subset of `args.includes("/claude")` (condition 4).
Additional Locations (2) - [`packages/plugins/agent-aider/src/index.ts#L101-L107`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/0be565ae9994c05a9f1814537cbad817756a708b/packages/plugins/agent-aider/src/index.ts#L101-L107) - [`packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts#L105-L111`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/0be565ae9994c05a9f1814537cbad817756a708b/packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts#L105-L111)

### Reactions never retry without state changes **High Severity** `executeReaction()` is only invoked inside the status-transition branch, so reactions run once when status first changes and never run again while the status stays the same. This prevents configured retry counting and time-based escalation in `lifecycle-manager.ts` for persistent states like `ci_failed` or `changes_requested`.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts#L397-L407`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/25826c0be3e8187b26a605587abe8036061f2bb1/packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts#L397-L407)

### Blocked sessions cannot recover to working **Medium Severity** When `agent.detectActivity()` returns active/idle and no PR state overrides apply, `determineStatus()` returns `session.status` (except `spawning`). Sessions in `needs_input` or `stuck` therefore remain pinned to those states even after the agent resumes normal activity.

### Project reaction overrides drop default fields **High Severity** `project.reactions` entries are `Partial`, but `checkSession()` uses them as full replacements via `??` instead of merging with `config.reactions`. If a project override sets only one field like `auto`, required fields like `action` can disappear, causing the reaction to never execute.

### Spawning without workspace breaks isolation **High Severity** `spawn()` validates `runtime` and `agent` plugins but not `workspace`. If `workspace` is unavailable, it silently uses `project.path` as `workspacePath`, so sessions run in the main repo instead of isolated workspaces. This can cause concurrent sessions to interfere with each other and persist unsafe metadata for later cleanup.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/core/src/session-manager.ts#L175-L191`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/25826c0be3e8187b26a605587abe8036061f2bb1/packages/core/src/session-manager.ts#L175-L191)

### AppleScript injection via unescaped session name in shell command **High Severity** The `shellSafe` variable (from `shellEscape`) is interpolated into an AppleScript double-quoted string without AppleScript escaping. `shellEscape` only handles single quotes for shell safety, so a session name containing `"` (e.g., from `runtimeHandle.id` or `session.id`) would break the AppleScript string delimiter in the `write text` command, enabling AppleScript injection. The `safe` variable is correctly escaped for AppleScript, but `shellSafe` needs both shell escaping *and* AppleScript escaping — applying `escapeAppleScript(shellEscape(sessionName))` would handle the layered quoting correctly.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/plugins/terminal-iterm2/src/index.ts#L98-L99`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/dea051b3bc56ffa181cc77c5f5c9b921a834d3c7/packages/plugins/terminal-iterm2/src/index.ts#L98-L99)

 

Triggered by project rule: BugBot Configuration

### Default dashboard port inconsistent with core config **Medium Severity** The default `dashboardUrl` uses port 9847 (`http://localhost:9847`), but the core config schema in `config.ts` defaults the dashboard port to 3000. This means terminal URLs generated by this plugin will point to the wrong port when using defaults, producing broken links that fail to connect.

### Falsy check conflates empty stdout with command failure **High Severity** The `git()` helper returns stdout on success and `null` on failure. Since `git worktree add -b` writes output to stderr (not stdout), a successful command returns an empty string `""`. The check `if (!result)` treats empty string as falsy, so the code always enters the fallback "branch already exists" path even when the first command succeeded. This triggers a second `git worktree add` that fails (worktree path already exists) and is silently swallowed. The correct check is `if (result === null)`.

### Shell injection via bash -c with interpolated string **Medium Severity** Calling `exec("bash", ["-c", ...])` with an interpolated `tty` variable inside a shell command string bypasses the security benefit of `execFile`. Although `tty` comes from tmux output and is typically safe, this pattern violates the project's security rule to prefer `execFile` over `exec` and avoid string concatenation in shell commands. The `tty` value is embedded in a double-quoted context inside a `bash -c` string, which could allow command injection if the value contained shell metacharacters.

 

Triggered by project rule: BugBot Configuration

### Batch-spawn duplicate detection uses stale tmux session list **Medium Severity** In `batch-spawn`, `allTmux` is captured once before the loop, but `findSessionForIssue` requires matching sessions to be in the `tmuxSessions` list (line 73 of `metadata.ts`). Newly spawned sessions within the same batch write metadata to disk but aren't in the stale `allTmux` list, so `findSessionForIssue` skips them during the `tmuxSessions.includes(name)` check. This means duplicate issue IDs passed in the same batch won't be detected, potentially spawning multiple sessions for the same issue.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/cli/src/lib/metadata.ts#L70-L73`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/cc11b3ec596be3b3ddd471f8eec3ee74ce742dc3/packages/cli/src/lib/metadata.ts#L70-L73)

### Substring matching causes false-positive duplicate issue detection **Medium Severity** `findSessionForIssue` uses `meta.issue.toLowerCase().includes(lower)` for matching, which is substring-based rather than exact equality. Searching for issue `"INT-1"` would false-positive match a session with issue `"INT-10"`, `"INT-100"`, or `"INT-12"`, since `"int-10".includes("int-1")` is `true`. This causes `batch-spawn` to incorrectly skip spawning sessions for legitimate new issues, silently reporting them as duplicates.

### Missing project validation crashes session ls and cleanup **Medium Severity** The `session ls` and `session cleanup` subcommands are missing the unknown-project validation that `status` and `review-check` have. When `--project nonexistent` is passed, `config.projects[opts.project]` is `undefined`, making the `projects` map contain `{ "nonexistent": undefined }`. Iterating it and accessing `project.sessionPrefix` on `undefined` throws an unhandled `TypeError`, crashing the CLI.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/cli/src/commands/session.ts#L118-L129`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/cc11b3ec596be3b3ddd471f8eec3ee74ce742dc3/packages/cli/src/commands/session.ts#L118-L129)

### `getPendingComments` returns resolved comments too **Medium Severity** The `SCM` interface documents `getPendingComments` as returning "pending (unresolved) review comments," but the implementation's `.filter()` only excludes bot authors — it never checks `t.isResolved`. All non-bot review threads are returned regardless of resolution status, violating the interface contract and potentially causing the orchestrator to treat already-resolved comments as outstanding work items.

### Duplicated `gh` helper across two plugin packages **Low Severity** The `gh` helper function (wrapping `execFileAsync` with identical error handling, timeout, and buffer config) is copy-pasted verbatim between `scm-github` and `tracker-github`. Maintaining two identical copies increases the risk of divergent bug fixes or inconsistent behavior when one copy is updated but not the other.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/plugins/tracker-github/src/index.ts#L24-L37`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/ae0eccdde9d8208ceb67fc26fd48fa62bb2ba084/packages/plugins/tracker-github/src/index.ts#L24-L37)

### Non-tmux runtimes return "idle" instead of "active" **Medium Severity** `detectActivity` returns `"idle"` for non-tmux runtimes (where `output` stays `null`), but returns `"active"` when tmux `capture-pane` throws an error. Both situations mean "process confirmed alive, no terminal output available," yet they produce different results. The `"idle"` state semantically means "agent is at prompt, waiting for input," which is an incorrect assertion when output simply isn't accessible. The `!output` null check was designed for the empty-tmux-pane case but inadvertently catches the non-tmux case too.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts#L374-L378`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/cf09b9b8c629d0a69e2900b10d425324a0753c06/packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts#L374-L378)

### Unguarded JSON.parse cast to JsonlLine type **Low Severity** `JSON.parse(trimmed) as JsonlLine` casts the parsed result without validating its shape. If a JSONL line contains a bare `null`, the cast hides the mismatch from TypeScript. Downstream in `extractCost`, accessing `line.costUSD` or `line.usage` on `null` would throw a `TypeError`, unlike `extractSummary` and `extractLastMessageType` which use optional chaining (`line?.type`). This violates the project rule about unguarded `JSON.parse`.

 

Triggered by project rule: BugBot Configuration

### Reaction escalation counts successful attempts **Medium Severity** `executeReaction()` increments `tracker.attempts` before execution and uses it for escalation regardless of outcome. Successful `send-to-agent` runs still increase retry counters, so repeated re-entry into the same state can escalate to human notifications even when auto-handling keeps succeeding.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts#L290-L305`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/580cebe63f4f0ba158fa84a598beca656da2a3c5/packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts#L290-L305)

### WORKING zone uses blue instead of specified green **Medium Severity** The `ok` (WORKING) zone's color is set to `var(--color-accent-blue)` but both the PR description and the architecture design doc (`artifacts/architecture-design.md` line 527: "**Green zone**: Sessions working normally") specify green. The color for the WORKING zone needs to be `var(--color-accent-green)` to match the design spec: URGENT=red, ACTION=orange, WARNING=yellow, WORKING=green, COMPLETED=grey.

### Redundant ternary always returns same value **Low Severity** The expression `session.pr ? "action" : "action"` in `getAttentionLevel` returns `"action"` in both branches, making the ternary dead logic. This looks like an incomplete implementation — perhaps the intent was to return a different level (like `"warning"` or `"ok"`) when there's no PR data for a session with `"mergeable"`/`"approved"` status.

### SSEEvent type is unused and structurally incorrect **Low Severity** The exported `SSEEvent` interface is never imported or referenced anywhere in the codebase. Additionally, its shape (`sessionId`, `priority`, `message`, `data` fields) doesn't match the actual SSE events produced by `/api/events/route.ts`, which emit `snapshot` events (with `sessions` array) and `session.activity` events (with `attentionLevel`, `timestamp`). This dead type with a wrong shape could mislead future consumers.

### Session ID not validated in kill and send routes **Medium Severity** The `id` URL parameter in the kill and send routes is used without validation. The spawn route validates user inputs with `validateIdentifier` (restricting to `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+`), but the session routes accept arbitrary strings. When wired to core services that execute shell commands (e.g., `tmux kill-session`), unsanitized session IDs could enable command injection.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/web/src/app/api/sessions/[id]/send/route.ts#L7-L9`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/04063f6f2b19c474c0b4c1bdd5ac4aa55438721d/packages/web/src/app/api/sessions/[id]/send/route.ts#L7-L9)

 

Triggered by project rule: BugBot Configuration

### PR discovery never happens from SCM **High Severity** `determineStatus()` only evaluates PR/CI/review logic when `session.pr` already exists. It never calls `scm.detectPR()`, so sessions that open a PR after spawn stay in `working` and never transition to `pr_open`/CI/review states unless metadata is updated elsewhere.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/core/src/types.ts#L344-L346`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/c9480255e727d815b7a012f547638ca08707c549/packages/core/src/types.ts#L344-L346)

### Summary events get wrong default priority **Low Severity** `inferPriority()` treats any event type containing `completed` as `action`. This causes `summary.all_complete` events created in `lifecycle-manager.ts` to default to `action` instead of `info`, which misclassifies completion summaries in event history and any consumers that rely on event priority.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts#L440-L446`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/c9480255e727d815b7a012f547638ca08707c549/packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts#L440-L446)

### Conflict and bot reactions never trigger **Medium Severity** `eventToReactionKey` defines reactions for `automated_review.found` and `merge.conflicts`, but `determineStatus` never checks `scm.getAutomatedComments` or conflict blockers and never emits those events. The configured `bugbot-comments` and `merge-conflicts` auto-reactions are therefore unreachable during lifecycle polling.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts#L92-L96`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/c26ed77b0b5e3fb5fe473e5235d10dc4544219bc/packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts#L92-L96)

### Branch checkout arguments are in wrong mode **High Severity** `git checkout` is invoked with `--` in a position that switches parsing to path mode, so branch checkout logic is incorrect. In `workspace-clone`, `create` tries `checkout -b --` and then `checkout --`, which prevents normal branch creation/checkout. The same fallback pattern appears in `workspace-worktree`.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/plugins/workspace-worktree/src/index.ts#L73-L74`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/16d7efb873c138fc04b50c31a3455233ac239429/packages/plugins/workspace-worktree/src/index.ts#L73-L74)

### Stale spawn error handler deletes live process **High Severity** The temporary `child.once("error")` listener used during spawn validation is never removed after success. If a later runtime `error` event occurs, it still runs `processes.delete(handleId)`, so a running process disappears from the map and subsequent `sendMessage`/`destroy` calls fail with “No process found”.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/plugins/runtime-process/src/index.ts#L94-L95`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/16d7efb873c138fc04b50c31a3455233ac239429/packages/plugins/runtime-process/src/index.ts#L94-L95)

### Worktree listing mixes similarly prefixed project IDs **Medium Severity** `list` filters entries with `path.startsWith(projectWorktreeDir)`, which also matches sibling directories that share the same prefix. Projects like `foo` and `foobar` can leak worktrees into each other’s results, returning incorrect `WorkspaceInfo` entries for the requested project.

### Concurrent tmux sends can paste wrong message **High Severity** Long-message delivery uses `load-buffer` and `paste-buffer` without a per-send buffer name. The default tmux buffer is shared, so concurrent `sendMessage` calls can overwrite each other between those two commands and paste the wrong content into a session.

### Symlink path can delete arbitrary filesystem paths **High Severity** `postCreate` trusts entries in `project.symlinks` and directly builds `targetPath` with `join`. Absolute or traversal values can resolve outside `info.path`, and the pre-symlink cleanup runs `rmSync` on that resolved path, allowing unintended deletion outside the workspace.

 

Triggered by project rule: BugBot Configuration

### Worktree removal prints success regardless of outcome **Low Severity** In `killSession`, the `git()` wrapper catches all errors and returns `null`, but the "Removed worktree" success message on the next line prints unconditionally. This contrasts with the tmux kill just above (lines 18–21), which correctly checks `killed !== null` before printing. Failed worktree removals will appear successful, potentially causing orphaned worktrees to accumulate without the user knowing.

### JSON output mode mixes decorative text with JSON **Medium Severity** When `--json` is passed, the banner (line 195), per-project headers (line 205), and footer summary (lines 231–236) are still printed as decorative text around the JSON arrays. This makes the output completely unparseable by `jq` or any JSON consumer. The `opts.json` flag only controls the per-project session rendering but doesn't suppress the surrounding non-JSON text.

### Missing error handler on browser-open spawn crashes dashboard **High Severity** The `spawn("open", ...)` call on line 83 has no `error` event listener. On non-macOS systems (Linux, Windows) where the `open` command doesn't exist, `spawn` emits an `ENOENT` `error` event. Per Node.js EventEmitter semantics, an unhandled `error` event throws and crashes the process — killing the running Next.js dashboard ~3 seconds after startup. This is the default behavior (`opts.open` is `true` unless `--no-open` is passed).

### Spinner never stopped when spawnSession throws mid-execution **Medium Severity** The `ora` spinner started on line 41 is never cleaned up if `spawnSession` throws (e.g., when `exec("tmux", ["new-session", ...])` fails on line 105). The spinner's internal `setInterval` keeps running. In `batch-spawn`, the error is caught on line 262 and the loop continues, so each failed spawn accumulates an orphaned spinner — garbling all subsequent terminal output and leaking timers.

### Stale errors in capture window misclassify idle as blocked **Medium Severity** The `detectActivity` method captures the last 15 lines of the tmux pane (`-S -15`) and checks patterns against the entire buffer. Since `BLOCKED_PATTERNS` is tested before `IDLE_PATTERNS`, a stale error message from earlier in the buffer (e.g., `Error: module not found`) will cause the agent to be classified as `"blocked"` even when it has recovered and is currently at an idle prompt (`❯`). The tests only verify "active overrides blocked" (line 471 of test file) but never test the "blocked + idle" co-occurrence, which will misclassify the agent and could trigger unnecessary lifecycle interventions.
Additional Locations (1) - [`packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts#L369-L372`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/e285f62df8a0842703b85d97286294e147aeddec/packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts#L369-L372)

### Web build failures no longer fail CI **High Severity** The `typecheck` job now ignores failures from `pnpm --filter @agent-orchestrator/web build` via `|| true`, so CI can pass even when the web app has real build or type errors. This removes CI protection for `@agent-orchestrator/web` while comments still state web is typechecked there.

### Draft PRs misclassified into warning attention zone **Medium Severity** `getAttentionLevel` doesn't consider `pr.isDraft` when evaluating PR review state. A draft PR typically has `reviewDecision: "none"`, which triggers the warning-zone return on line 194. This causes actively-working sessions with draft PRs (like `frontend-6` in mock data, explicitly commented as "OK") to appear in the WARNING zone instead of the OK/WORKING zone.

This is by design and inherent to the process runtime model. Unlike tmux sessions which persist independently, child processes spawned via `spawn()` are tied to the orchestrator's process tree. When the orchestrator restarts, those child processes are gone (or orphaned by the OS) — there is no way to "reconnect" to an arbitrary `ChildProcess` by PID after restart.

This is exactly why the tmux runtime exists as the default: tmux sessions survive orchestrator restarts and can be reattached. The process runtime is intended for short-lived, ephemeral workloads where persistence across restarts is not needed.

The `RuntimeHandle.data.pid` field is available for callers that need to implement external cleanup (e.g., `kill <pid>`), but reconnection is not possible at the Node.js `ChildProcess` API level.

**Problem:** The `model` field was added to `SessionMetadata` type and set during `spawn()`, but `writeMetadata()` and `readMetadata()` were never updated to actually serialize/deserialize it. 1. **In readMetadata()** (line 95):
```typescript
model: raw["model"],
```

2. **In writeMetadata()** (line 136):
```typescript
if (metadata.model) data["model"] = metadata.model;
```

Now the model field is properly persisted to disk during spawn and correctly restored from metadata, eliminating reliance on project config fallback.

### Suffix matching resolves to wrong tmux session **High Severity** The `endsWith("-{sessionId}")` suffix match in `resolveTmuxSession` is ambiguous and can connect users to the wrong terminal session. The API contract in `AgentLaunchConfig` states that `systemPromptFile` "takes precedence over systemPrompt" when set, meaning `systemPrompt` should be ignored. Both `agent-aider` and `agent-claude-code` implement this correctly using `else if` to ensure mutual exclusion. The Cline plugin uses separate `if` statements, causing both to be concatenated into the final prompt, which violates the documented behavior and could lead to duplicate or conflicting system prompts being passed to the agent.

### Missing validation allows NaN PID return **Medium Severity** The `parseInt(cols[0] ?? "0", 10)` call on line 244 lacks validation to ensure it returns a valid number. If the PID column in `ps` output is malformed or non-numeric, `parseInt` returns `NaN`. Since `NaN !== null` evaluates to `true`, the `isProcessRunning` method incorrectly returns `true` for a non-existent process. This causes the orchestrator to believe an agent is running when it has actually terminated or never started, preventing proper cleanup and session state transitions. The function should validate the parsed result with `Number.isFinite()` before returning, similar to the validation on line 253 for the process runtime path.

### sessionFileMatchesCwd reads entire file despite documentation **Medium Severity** `sessionFileMatchesCwd` reads the entire file into memory but documentation claims it reads only the first 4KB. This causes unnecessary memory usage and I/O when scanning for matching session files, especially problematic with large rollout files. The function only uses the first 10 lines but loads everything.

### Race condition in binary resolution **Low Severity** `postLaunchSetup` has a check-then-act race condition where concurrent calls can both see `resolvedBinary` as null and both execute `resolveCodexBinary()`, wasting resources by resolving the binary path multiple times.

### Concurrent connect calls cause process leak **High Severity** `connect()` has a check-then-act race condition where concurrent calls spawn multiple processes. The second spawn overwrites `this.process`, orphaning the first process with no way to kill it. This causes a resource leak of child processes that continue running indefinitely.

### connect failure leaves resources uncleaned **Medium Severity** If `initialize()` throws during `connect()`, the spawned process and readline interface are left running without cleanup. The caller must explicitly call `close()` after a failed `connect()`, which is non-intuitive and error-prone.

### readline interface not closed on process exit **Medium Severity** `handleProcessExit` and `handleProcessError` don't close the readline interface, leaving it attached to the closed stdout stream. This resource leak prevents proper cleanup when the process exits unexpectedly, keeping event listeners active indefinitely.

### stderr pipe not consumed causes child blocking **High Severity** The spawned process pipes stderr but never consumes it. If the `codex app-server` writes enough to stderr, the buffer fills and the child process blocks waiting for the pipe to drain, causing the client to hang indefinitely.

### Binary resolve guard gets stuck on rejection **Medium Severity** `postLaunchSetup()` caches the in-flight `resolveCodexBinary()` promise in `resolvingBinary`, but if `resolveCodexBinary()` rejects, the code never clears `resolvingBinary`. Later calls keep awaiting the same rejected promise, so binary resolution can never recover within that agent instance.

### Merge steward merge may fail in detached worktree **Medium Severity** When `mergeMethod` is `"merge"`, the merge uses `options.sourceBranch` directly. The merge is discarded, yet the function returns `{ merged: true, tempWorktreePath }` with a path that no longer exists. Callers are told the merge succeeded even though nothing was persisted.

The `gh pr create` matcher requires `([[:space:]]|$)` after `create`, so a chained command like `gh pr create; ...` or `gh pr create&& ...` (no space) will no longer match. If the goal is to support command chaining with `;`, `&`, and `&&`, consider allowing those delimiters (or a general non-word boundary) after `create` rather than only whitespace/end-of-string.
```suggestion
if [[ "$command" =~ (^|[;&][[:space:]]*|&&[[:space:]]*)gh[[:space:]]+pr[[:space:]]+create([[:space:];&]|$) ]]; then
```

The `git checkout -b` pattern captures the branch with `([^[:space:]]+)`. With the newly-supported `;` / `&` chaining, a command like `git checkout -b foo; gh ...` (no space before `;`) will capture `foo;` as the branch. Consider excluding common command delimiters from the capture group and/or adding a post-branch boundary so separators aren’t included in the branch value.

Same issue as above for `git switch -c`: `([^[:space:]]+)` can capture delimiters when chaining without spaces (e.g. `git switch -c foo&& gh ...`), leading to an incorrect `branch` metadata value. Tighten the capture group and/or require a delimiter/whitespace boundary after the branch name.

The `git checkout <branch>` matcher can also capture trailing command delimiters when chaining without spaces (e.g. `git checkout feature/foo; ...`), since the branch group doesn’t stop at `;`/`&`. Consider stopping the capture at common separators and/or adding an explicit boundary after the branch token.

The `gh pr merge` matcher has the same `([[:space:]]|$)` suffix as `gh pr create`, which will fail to match chained invocations like `gh pr merge; ...` or `gh pr merge&& ...` without a space. If chaining delimiters are intended to be supported, allow `;`/`&`/`&&` as valid terminators here too.
```suggestion
if [[ "$command" =~ (^|[;&][[:space:]]*|&&[[:space:]]*)gh[[:space:]]+pr[[:space:]]+merge([[:space:];&]|$) ]]; then
```

Same delimiter-capture risk applies to the `git switch <branch>` matcher: without an explicit boundary after the branch token, chaining like `git switch feature/foo&& ...` can include `&&` in the captured branch. Adjust the capture/boundary to stop at common separators (`;`, `&`, `&&`, etc.).

### Shell syntax error: semicolon after `then` keyword **High Severity** The array of shell command fragments is joined with `"; "`, which places a semicolon immediately after the `then` keyword in the `if/then/fi` construct, producing `if [ -z "$SES_ID" ]; then; SES_ID=$(...)`. ### Stale fetch can overwrite state after project switch **Medium Severity** When the user switches projects, the EventSource effect cleanup closes the old connection but does not cancel the in-flight `fetch` triggered by a membership mismatch. The pending `fetch` carries the old `project` value in its closure. If it resolves *after* the new project's `initialSessions` reset, its `dispatch({ type: "reset" })` overwrites the state with stale sessions from the wrong project.
